newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malacanang has asked Transportation Secretary Luis Lagdameo to tender his resignation before the Holy Week is over. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Manila Archbishop Jaime Cardinal Sin accused anew yesterday National Security Adviser General Jose Almonte of manipulating groups seeking to amend the 1987 Constitution to give President Fidel Ramos a chance to run for a second term. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- President Fidel Ramos on Sunday called for an in-depth study of a controversial four-point proposal, including arrests without warrants of suspects to curb kidnapping for ransom activities. The proposal was drawn up by the Presidential Anti-Crime Commission. (MANILA STANDARD)
- The Philippine Central Bank will look into the credit card and auto loan exposure of the banking sector as prelimianry indications point to rising credit defaults in these areas. (INQUIRER)

- At least three member brokers of the Philippine Stock Exchange may have violated rules on insider trading and price manipulation, but their investigations were terminated or put on hold early this year. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The Tariff Commission has recommended the reduction of tariff on sugar from the current 100 percent to 80 percent by July this year. (BUSINESSWORLD)
